section_1.title: The Problem: Why Traditional Models Fail
section_1.content: Introduce the limitation of RNNs (processing words linearly) which causes 'forgetting' at the end of long sentences. Contrast this with human reading, where we jump across sentences to connect related ideas.
section_1.example: In the sentence: 'The animal didn't cross the street because it was too tired,' humans instantly know 'it' refers to the 'animal'. Older models lose context after just a few words.

section_2.title: The Core Concept: Query, Key, and Value
section_2.content: Introduce the retrieval analogy. Query (what I'm looking for), Key (what I have to offer), and Value (the actual information). Use a visual search icon for Q, a label tag for K, and a document icon for V.
section_2.example: Imagine a library: Your 'Query' is the search term, the book 'Key' is the title on the spine, and the 'Value' is the content inside the book.

section_3.title: The Math: Dot Product and Softmax
section_3.content: Explain how we calculate relevance: Dot product (Q·K^T) measures similarity (alignment). Softmax converts scores into percentages (attention weights). Visual: Heatmap matrix showing stronger connections as brighter colors.
section_3.example: If Query is 'Animal' and Key is 'Tired', the dot product is high. If Query is 'Animal' and Key is 'Street', the dot product is low. Softmax ensures these weights sum to 100%.

section_4.title: Multi-Head Attention: Seeing the Big Picture
section_4.content: Explain that one 'head' isn't enough to understand complex language. We use multiple heads in parallel to focus on different aspects like grammar, sentiment, and entity relationships.
section_4.example: Think of a team of analysts: Head 1 looks for grammar, Head 2 looks for the subject, Head 3 looks for emotional tone. Combining these gives a rich, multi-dimensional understanding.

section_5.title: Summary and Application
section_5.content: Recap how attention transforms raw text into a mathematical map of relationships, enabling LLMs to 'pay attention' to relevant words regardless of distance.
section_5.example: When you ask ChatGPT to summarize a 50-page document, the Attention mechanism allows it to jump directly to the most relevant paragraphs while ignoring filler words.
